title: Nonzero relative differential gives a smooth hypersurface point
statement: Let $p:W\to S$ be a smooth morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], let $\mathcal M$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_W$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], let $s\in\Gamma(W,\mathcal M)$, and let $Z=Z(s)\subseteq W$ be its zero scheme [def-pc-zero-scheme]. Fix $z\in Z$ and a trivialization of $\mathcal M$ near $z$, writing $s=f$ there. Let $df(z)$ denote the image of the universal relative differential of $f$ in $\Omega^1_{W/S,z}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{W,z}}\kappa(z)$ [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf, def-weil-residue-field]. If $df(z)\ne0$, then $Z\to S$ is smooth at $z$, meaning that it is smooth on some open neighbourhood of $z$ in $Z$. No flatness assumption on $Z\to S$ is required.

source.place: Tag 00T7, lemma-standard-smooth, (1), applied after adjoining one equation with an extra nonzero Jacobian row to a standard smooth presentation (Definition 00T6, definition-standard-smooth); smooth charts are Morphisms Tag 01V7, lemma-smooth-locally-standard-smooth.

proof.text: Let $W_0$ be the given trivializing open neighbourhood of $z$. The restriction $W_0\to S$ is smooth by [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-locally-standard-smooth] to obtain affine neighbourhoods $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset W_0$ of $z$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S$ of $p(z)$, with $p(U)\subset V$ and $A$ standard smooth over $R$. Write $s|_U=f$ in the restricted trivialization. By [lem-pc-zero-scheme-properties], $Z\cap U=\operatorname{Spec}B$, where $B=A/(f)$. Let $\mathfrak q\subset A$ be the prime of $z$; it contains $f$. Choose a presentation $A=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(g_1,\ldots,g_c)$ as in [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra], and write $a_i$ for the class of $x_i$. The matrix $J=(\partial_i g_\ell)_{1\le\ell,i\le c}$ over $A$ has unit determinant (it is the transpose of the matrix in that definition).

By [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf], the restriction of $\Omega^1_{W/S}$ to $U$ is $\widetilde{\Omega_{A/R}}$, carrying $d_{W/S}f$ to the universal $df$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-stalk-localization] and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], its stalk at $z$ is $(\Omega_{A/R})_{\mathfrak q}$ over $A_{\mathfrak q}=\mathcal O_{W,z}$. Thus the vector in the hypothesis is $df\otimes1$ in $\Omega_{A/R}\otimes_A\kappa(z)$: the identification sends $(\omega/u)\otimes\lambda$ to $\omega\otimes(\bar u^{-1}\lambda)$, with inverse $\omega\otimes\lambda\mapsto(\omega/1)\otimes\lambda$. By [lem-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-kahler-basis], $da_{c+1},\ldots,da_n$ form an $A$-basis. Write $df=\sum_{i>c}b_i\,da_i$. Tensoring this finite free module gives $\kappa(z)^{n-c}$ with those basis vectors. Nonvanishing therefore gives an index $j>c$ with $b_j\notin\mathfrak q$. In particular $n>c$; the case $n=c$ cannot satisfy the hypothesis.

Choose a polynomial $h\in R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ mapping to $f$. All partial derivatives in this step are evaluated at $(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$. Put $k_i=(\partial_i g_\ell)_{\ell=1}^c$ for $i>c$ and $u=(\partial_1h,\ldots,\partial_ch)$. The derivation rules of [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], applied to monomials and then sums, give $dG(a)=\sum_i(\partial_iG)(a)\,da_i$ for any polynomial $G$. Apply this to $g_\ell(a)=0$. In column notation the resulting identities are $J(da_1,\ldots,da_c)^{\mathrm t}=-\sum_{i>c}k_i\,da_i$. Since $J^{-1}=(\det J)^{-1}\operatorname{adj}(J)$ exists, substitute into $df=dh(a)$ to obtain
$$b_i=\partial_i h-uJ^{-1}k_i\quad(i>c).$$
These are the coefficients of Step 2 by uniqueness in its cited basis; no exactness or flatness of a tensor functor has been used.

source.place: Tag 00T6 (definition-standard-smooth), enlarged minor for the extra equation; block determinant calculation supplied explicitly

proof.text:
Put $C=B[1/\delta]$, the localization of [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. It has the explicit $R$-algebra presentation
$$C\cong R[x_1,\ldots,x_n,t]/(g_1,\ldots,g_c,h,t\Delta-1).$$
Indeed, send $x_i$ to the image of $a_i$ and $t$ to $\delta^{-1}$. Conversely the classes of $x_i$ induce a map from $B$, and $t\Delta=1$ makes $\delta$ invertible, so it extends to $C$. These maps fix every generator in either direction and are inverse. Order the variables with $x_1,\ldots,x_c,x_j,t$ first; these are $c+2$ distinct variables since $j>c$. The Jacobian of the $c+2$ equations with respect to these variables has upper-right column zero and bottom-right entry $\Delta$, while its upper-left $(c+1)$-square block has determinant $\Delta$. Its determinant is therefore $\Delta^2$, a unit in $C$. Thus this presentation is standard smooth by [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra]. The inequality on the numbers of equations and variables is $c+2\le n+1$, which holds because $n>c$.

source.place: Tag 00T6 (definition-standard-smooth); explicit localization presentation as in Example 00T8 (example-make-standard-smooth)

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-is-smooth], $C$ is smooth over $R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine], $\operatorname{Spec}C\to V$ is smooth. By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion], $\operatorname{Spec}C=D_B(\delta)$ is an open subscheme of $\operatorname{Spec}B=Z\cap U$, containing $z$ by Step 4. It is consequently an open neighbourhood of $z$ in $Z$. Its composite to $S$ is smooth in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]: local finite presentation is checked using the same affine target neighbourhood $V\subset S$. For formal smoothness, any first order thickening $T\subset T'$ of affine schemes over $S$ with $T\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ has $T'\to S$ factoring through $V$, because $T$ and $T'$ have the same underlying topological space and $T$ maps into $V$. The smooth map $\operatorname{Spec}C\to V$ supplies the required lift of $T\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ over $V$, hence over $S$. This proves smoothness on the exhibited open neighbourhood, with no assumed flatness of $B$ or $Z\to S$.
